note.text:
Pattern recognition means finding what is the same, or what repeats, in problems and data. Once we see a pattern we can predict what comes next and reuse a solution.
Number patterns: 3, 7, 11, 15, … adds 4 each time, so the next number is 19. 2, 4, 8, 16, … doubles each time.
Shape patterns: circle, square, triangle, circle, square, triangle, … repeats every three shapes.
To find a far-away shape in a repeating pattern, divide its position by the length of the pattern and look at the remainder.
Patterns are everywhere: the days of the week, school timetables, the seasons, the numbers on a calendar.

worked_example.problem: What are the next two numbers in the pattern {firstTerms(a, d, 4)}, …?
steps: Find the difference between neighbours: {a + d} − {a} = {d}.

cards.idea: Pattern recognition is finding what is the same or what repeats.
In a number pattern, look at how each number changes: add the same amount, or double.
A repeating pattern repeats a group of shapes; find the group, then continue it.
example: Circle, square, circle, square: the group is “circle, square”.

misconceptions.explain: Find the group of shapes that repeats, then continue it.

solution: The group that repeats has {patternLength(p)} shapes.

questions.prompt: What is the next number? {firstTerms(a, d, 4)}, …

misconceptions.explain: Find how much is added each time: {d}.

solution: Each number is {d} more than the one before.

misconceptions.explain: Find the group of shapes that repeats, then continue it.

solution: The group that repeats has {patternLength(p)} shapes.

misconceptions.explain: The numbers do not go up by the same amount: each one is double the one before.

solution: Each number is double the one before.

questions.prompt: This pattern keeps repeating. What is shape number {n}?

misconceptions.explain: Divide the position by the length of the group and use the remainder.

solution: The group has {patternLength(p)} shapes. {n} ÷ {patternLength(p)} = {idiv(n, patternLength(p))} remainder {n % patternLength(p)}.
{n % patternLength(p) == 0 ? 'Remainder 0 means the last shape of the group' : 'Remainder ' + (n % patternLength(p)) + ' means shape number ' + (n % patternLength(p)) + ' of the group'}: {answer}.

questions.prompt: The pattern {firstTerms(a, d, 4)}, … continues. What is number {n} in the pattern?

misconceptions.explain: The first number has no {d} added yet: add {d} only {n - 1} times.

solution: The first number is {a}; each one adds {d}.
